checksums.name: selection_record_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: Unsigned additive sum of all 16 record bytes (offsets 0x0-0xF relative to record start) computed with the 4-byte checksum field (relative offset 0x8-0xB) temporarily zeroed; stored back into that field as a little-endian u32. No modulo/wraparound masking, no XOR, no CRC, no seed. Implemented by FUN_0801296c; constructed by FUN_0801278c; verified by FUN_080125b0.

checksums.name: selection_record_checksum_mirror_b
checksums.formula_detail: Identical algorithm and field layout as selection_record_checksum, applied to the second mirror copy at offset 0x7F10.

checksums.name: main_save_record_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: Same additive-sum primitive (FUN_0801296c) as the selection record, but covering the entire 0x7C0 (1984) byte record with the 4-byte checksum field at relative offset 0x4-0x7 zeroed during summation. Verified by FUN_0801256c. Not observed as non-erased in either supplied .sav; cannot be verified against real bytes.

io_driver_functions.notes: Copy primitive used for both the small (0x10) and large (0x7c0) record reads; call-site argument ordering/sizes trusted, but the decompiled loop body is explicitly flagged by the tool as unreliable due to overlapping-global-symbol corruption. Preceded by a 16-bit read-mask-OR-3 register write structurally consistent with (but not literally confirmed as) GBA WAITCNT SRAM wait-state configuration.

Byte-copy write primitive for the small 16-byte record, RAM scratch buffer -> SRAM mirror destination. Same &mask|3 register idiom precedes the copy loop; this loop body is not flagged with the overlap warning, so its shape is more trusted than 0x080f482c's.
Write-verify readback counterpart to 0x080f4890, invoked immediately after each write in a retry loop (max 5 attempts); delegates comparison to func_0x080f49a8 (undecompiled stub).
The sole checksum primitive in this corpus: unsigned additive sum of len bytes starting at ptr, returned as an unmasked 32-bit value. Used identically by both the small and large record formats.

Writer for the small 16-byte 'MOTSEL12' selection record. No caller of this function exists among the 158 extracted functions in this corpus, so the real-world value(s) of its param_1 argument (stored at relative offset 0xC) are unknown.

Validator/reader for the small 16-byte record: checks 'MOTSEL12' magic, zeroes the checksum field, recomputes the sum via 0x0801296c, compares to the stored value. Returns 0=ok, 1=checksum mismatch, 2=bad magic.

Top-level reader for the small record: tries mirror A, falls back to mirror B on validation failure, returns the record's offset-0xC field on success or 0xFFFFFFFF on total failure. No caller found in this corpus.
Validator/reader for the large 0x7C0-byte record: checks 'MOT2' magic, zeroes the 4-byte checksum field, recomputes sum via 0x0801296c over the whole record, compares to stored value.

Top-level reader for the large record: computes two mirror SRAM offsets from a slot index read from a RAM source struct, tries mirror A then mirror B, returns success/failure. No caller found in this corpus. No writer for this record was found anywhere in the 158 extracted functions.
Initializes globals for the large-record subsystem: stores the 0x7C0 record-size constant and a base pointer. Not itself a writer of record bytes.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one bit (e.g. XOR 0x01) in mirror A's checksum only, leave mirror B intact
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Mirror A fails FUN_080125b0 validation (checksum mismatch, code 1); FUN_080124c4 falls back to mirror B, which still validates; no externally observable change expected until the next write resynchronizes both mirrors.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Zero out the checksum field in BOTH mirrors (0x7F08 and 0x7F18)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Both mirror validations fail; FUN_080124c4 returns total failure (*param_1 = 0xFFFFFFFF); downstream UI consuming the selection value should fall back to a default/no-selection state.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change the first magic byte (0x7F00, 'M') to any other value, mirror A only
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Mirror A fails validation with bad-magic code (2) instead of checksum-mismatch code (1); both should be externally indistinguishable since the caller only checks != 0, falling back to mirror B.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Sweep the 0xC field (both mirrors) through 0x00000001, 0x00000002, 0x00000003, ... with checksum repair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this field selects a save slot/character/difficulty, the title screen or load menu should visibly change its default selection when reloading from a title-screen save state; no observable change for any value would narrow (not confirm) the field's hypothesized role.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Perform an in-game action expected to trigger a real game save (not just the title-screen selection captured here), then re-dump SRAM and diff against the blank baseline
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: A new non-erased 0x7C0-byte range (or two, 0x7C0/0xF80 apart per the mirror-offset formula) should appear, beginning with ASCII 'MOT2' and containing a valid sum32 checksum at relative offset +4, locating the large record for the first time.

Absolute SRAM offset of the large 'MOT2' / 0x7C0-byte record; base global _DAT_080124b4 is unresolved in this corpus.

No writer function for the large 'MOT2' record was found among the 158 extracted functions; it is CONFIRMED_STATIC as a read/validate format only.

Exact hardware register touched by the repeated '&mask|3' idiom in FUN_080f482c/FUN_080f4890 is structurally consistent with GBA WAITCNT SRAM wait-state bits but not literally confirmed; no literal 0x04000204 constant appears in this corpus.

ghidra/callgraph.json resolved zero static call edges for every function discussed in this report; all caller/callee relationships were reconstructed manually from ghidra/decompiled.c, which introduces human-tracing risk despite the byte-level checksum cross-check.

No paired .ss emulator save states were supplied for this release (states/ is empty for this legacy checkpoint cohort), so the fuzzing plan's predicted gameplay/UI effects have not been executed, only specified.
